rules.title: Tenant screening fee limits (Civil Code 1950.6)
rules.requirement: Landlords may charge a screening fee, capped at $68.96 for 2026, to obtain information such as a consumer credit report. The applicant should receive a copy of the credit report within 7 days of the landlord's receipt, a receipt with an itemized list of out-of-pocket expenses and time spent, and a refund of any unused portion; the landlord must use a reusable screening report if the tenant provides one.
rules.coverage_text: Landlords charging prospective tenants a screening fee
rules.quoted_span: Prospective tenants should expect to receive a copy of their credit report within 7 days of receipt by the landlord, a receipt for the fee paid and an itemized list of any out-of-pocket expenses and time spent by the landlord on the screening, and a refund of any unused portion of the fee. If the tenant provides a reusable screening report, the landlord must use it.

rules.title: No screening fee without available unit; return of fee to applicants not selected (Civil Code 1950.6)
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot charge a screening fee if no rental unit is actually available. The landlord must return the fee to any applicant not selected, or have a policy of reviewing applications in the order received, giving the unit to the first qualified applicant, and not charging applicants who are not considered.
rules.coverage_text: Landlords charging prospective tenants a screening fee
rules.quoted_span: The landlord cannot charge a prospective tenant a screening fee if no rental unit is actually available. The landlord must also return a screening fee to any applicant not selected, or have a policy under which they: (1) review applications in the order received and the first qualified applicant gets the unit, and (2) do not charge a screening fee to any applicant not considered.

rules.title: Notification of state law limitation on tenant screening fees
rules.requirement: An owner or agent who charges an applicant a fee for a consumer credit report or to process an application must provide, in the rental application or a separate disclosure before receiving the fee, a clear and conspicuous Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement and a statement of the maximum fee cap permitted under Civil Code Section 1950.6(b).
rules.coverage_text: Owners or agents of residential property in Berkeley who charge applicants a screening or application processing fee

rules.title: Prohibition of non-refundable application fees associated with existing tenancies
rules.requirement: An owner or agent of residential rental property cannot charge an existing tenant a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy, including fees tied to a roommate's departure or a request to add or replace a roommate.
rules.coverage_text: Owners of residential rental property in Berkeley (or their agents) and existing tenants; applies to all residential rental agreements regardless of contrary lease language
rules.quoted_span: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part, including any fee associated with the departure of a roommate or to request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.
